synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the PR fixes a real bug (the old `s.stack = s.stack[0:]` was a no-op that left stale stack contents across Sort() calls) and moves cleanup to a defer block, which is the right direction. However, the diff bundles three independent changes — state-machine collapse from four states to three, deferred cleanup of state and stack, and a subtle relocation of `state[k] = sorted` inside the yield-success branch — without documenting the new invariants or proving the state collapse preserves semantics. The renamed `walking` state is now load-bearing for cycle detection in push() but its meaning (covers both 'children being expanded' and 'on-stack ancestor') is undocumented. The replacement comment introduces two spelling errors ('visisted', 'its') and is vaguer than what it replaces, and no regression test was added for the reuse bug the PR exists to fix. Verdict: correct mechanism, missing specification work and test coverage.

issues.description: State machine collapse from four states to three is undocumented; `walking` now carries load-bearing semantics for cycle detection
issues.detail: The old code had unsorted/working/walking/sorted; the PR removes `working` and reuses `walking` for what `working` used to mean (children pushed, awaiting second visit). The push() function's cycle-detection branch (which uses slicesx.LastIndexFunc to locate the node on the stack) now fires on this renamed state. The collapse may be correct, but the diff does not document the new state machine, does not prove the two former states are indistinguishable, and the name `walking` is misleading because it is set before descent rather than during walk-back. Add a comment block above the const block naming the three states (unsorted = not yet visited; walking = on stack with children being expanded; sorted = yielded) and the transition triggers, or rename to something honest like `onStack`/`entered`.

issues.description: Assignment of `state[k] = sorted` moved inside the yield-success branch — silent semantic change bundled with refactor
issues.detail: Previously `s.state[k] = sorted` ran unconditionally after the pop, even when yield returned false. Now it runs only inside the `if state != sorted` block and only when yield returns true. The previous postcondition 'after pop, state[k] == sorted' no longer holds at early-return. This is observationally safe under the new defer-clear, but it is a real semantic change buried in what looks like cleanup. Either call it out explicitly in the commit message as a separate fix (the old code marked nodes sorted on early termination, which was a latent bug), or hoist the assignment back outside to preserve the simpler invariant.

issues.description: PR bundles three independent changes — split into separate patches
issues.detail: The diff combines (1) state-machine collapse from four to three states (refactor), (2) fix to the no-op `s.stack = s.stack[0:]` reset by moving to deferred `s.stack[:0]` (real bug fix — the old line did nothing), and (3) deferred `clear(s.state)` for cross-call cleanup (correctness fix for Sorter reuse). These have independent justifications and risk profiles. Land as three patches so a future bisect can blame the right one, and so each can be justified and reviewed on its own terms.

issues.description: Sort() contract (preconditions, postconditions, invariants, termination) is not written down
issues.detail: The Sorter ADT exposes Sort() returning iter.Seq[Node] but does not document: the precondition (no concurrent Sort iteration), the postcondition (state and stack cleared on completion or early termination), the loop invariant relating s.stack, s.state, and the unyielded portion of the DAG, or the termination function. The cleanup-on-defer also changes the lifecycle — state is no longer inspectable after iteration completes. Without a written invariant, no one can verify the state collapse preserves correctness or that the deferred cleanup matches the intended contract. Add a contract block above Sort() and a comment naming the loop invariant.

issues.description: No regression test added for the state-reuse bug being fixed
issues.detail: The PR title is 'Fix state reuse' but contains no test that calls Sort() twice on the same Sorter (with the second call exercising stale state the old code left behind) and demonstrates the old code produces wrong output while the new code is correct. A test covering both back-to-back completion and early-termination-via-yield-returning-false would pin the contract and prevent regression. Without it, future refactors will reintroduce the bug unnoticed.

issues.description: Replacement comment has two typos and is vaguer than what it replaced
issues.detail: The new comment reads 'whether this node has been visisted and if its the first or second visit'. 'visisted' should be 'visited'; 'its' should be 'it's'. More importantly, this is the load-bearing explanation of the two-pass DFS and the right place to name the three states and their transitions explicitly (unsorted -> walking on first visit/push children -> sorted on second visit/emit). Rewrite to spell correctly and to name the state machine inline.

issues.description: Deferred `clear(s.stack)` + reslice to `[:0]` needs a comment explaining why both calls exist
issues.detail: `clear(s.stack)` zeroes entries in the backing array so retained Node references can be GC'd, then `s.stack = s.stack[:0]` resets length while preserving capacity. Both are needed for the pointer-holding-pool idiom, but a future maintainer will be tempted to delete one as redundant. Add a one-line comment: 'clear zeroes entries so Nodes can be collected; the reslice keeps capacity for reuse'. Torvalds notes the order could also be argued (reslice then clear the tail) — pick one and document the intent.
